title: E2 Window sweep: honest false rejects vs replay / delayed relay
notes: A4 uses attacker delay D = 30 s.

"before" = the relay reached the server before any later owner counter was accepted. Those relays carry a fresh counter and are expected to pass for every W: an irreducible floor of SDM counter checking.
Honest rates are per delivered message; messages within one trial are not independent, so the Wilson interval is somewhat optimistic.

Time rule T (a condition, not a recommendation): T only helps when honest upload delays are much shorter than attacker delays. A late honest upload and a delayed relay both carry an older counter; the server can only tell them apart by how late they arrive.

config._readme: All simulation parameters live here. Fields whose name starts with '_' are notes, not parameters. Every value marked ASSUMPTION is a modeling choice, not a measurement - change it and re-run, never tune it to make results look better.

tag._note: Tag model per NXP AN12196 (SUN MAC). macBits = 64 is the real NTAG 424 DNA truncated MAC; smaller values are only for experiment E1.
tag._tamperInMac: DEPLOYMENT REQUIREMENT (NXP NT4H2421Tx (NTAG 424 DNA TT) product data sheet, Rev. 3.0, 31 Jan 2019, Doc. 465530, Sec. 9.3.4-9.3.5): the SDMMAC covers the file data from SDMMACInputOffset to SDMMACOffset - 1, and the tamper status is mirrored at TTStatusOffset. The MAC protects the tamper status only if the tag is configured with TTStatusOffset inside that range. true = such a tag; false = a tag configured without it.
tag._tamperStatusFormat: MODEL SIMPLIFICATION: the chip mirrors two ASCII characters, TTPermStatus || TTCurrStatus, each C (closed), O (open) or I (invalid: tamper feature not enabled) (data sheet Sec. 9.3.5, 10.2). The model mirrors one C/O character and assumes the tamper feature is enabled.
tag._plaintextMirroring: ASSUMPTION: UID and counter are mirrored as plain hex text (not the encrypted PICCData mode).

verifier._note: Default server policy, used by E3 (as one of the selected settings), E4, A1 and A5. W = backward window, T = time rule in seconds (null = off).

rateLimit._note: ASSUMPTION: at most 10 verification attempts per tag per 60 s (sliding window). Failed MAC checks count.

owner._note: Default owner = the 'steady' scenario. ASSUMPTION: an honest owner taps tapsPerTrial times; gaps between taps are exponential with mean meanTapGapSeconds.

scenarios._note: E2, E3 and E4 are run once per scenario. Each scenario replaces fields of 'owner' (and may set its own attacker delays for E4).

steady.label: Steady taps (every ~60 s)
steady._note: Comparison scenario: one owner tapping on average every 60 s, 20 taps per trial.

gold.label: Gold sales (bursts, quiet days to weeks)
gold._note: ASSUMPTION: a gold bar changes hands in sales. In each sale the seller and buyer tap 2-4 times in total, a few minutes apart (random gaps, 90 s on average). Between sales the bar sits in storage for 1-28 days. Each trial covers 6 sales. Attackers who need the bar in hand act only during a sale or up to 2 minutes after its last tap. (Fields: tapsPerSale, meanGapWithinSaleSeconds, quietGapDays, salesPerTrial, captureTailSeconds.)

channel._note: ASSUMPTION (not measured): each honest upload is lost with probability pLoss; otherwise delayed by a uniform base delay, plus, with probability pReorder, an extra delay large enough to arrive after later uploads.

A1._note: Clone: same UID, different (random) key, fresh counter. One clone message per trial at a random moment during the owner's activity.

A2._note: Replay: resubmits a previously accepted owner message after a uniform delay.

A3._note: MAC guessing: chosen fresh counter, random MAC, attempts spaced so the rate limit never blocks them (the best a patient attacker can do).

A4._note: Delayed relay: attacker taps the genuine tag at a random moment of the owner's activity, keeps the message, submits it D seconds later. Server-side this is identical to intercepting an upload that never arrives.

A5._note: Tamper-flag forgery: the seal is open; attacker taps, changes 'open' to 'closed', submits with the unchanged MAC or a random guessed MAC.

experiments._scenarios: Scenarios used by E2, E3 and E4 (keys of 'scenarios').

E5._note: Floor formula check (steady scenario only; the formula assumes Poisson taps). Run at the normal trial length and at a long one, to show the end-of-trial effect.
